title: Quantile SLI decomposition & trace anchors for multi-tenant inference
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight playbook for decomposing SLI regressions using quantile-based views and trace-anchor grouping. Focus is on multi-tenant inference where a small subset of tenants or request shapes drives high tail latency/cost. The goal is to provide a reproducible investigation flow (dashboards + traces + queries) that surfaces high-impact contributors without requiring full-cardinality retention.

High-level goals:
- Make 95/99/99.9 quantile regressions actionable by mapping them to tenant/model/request-shape groups.
- Use trace anchors (span-pattern fingerprints) to cluster slow tail behavior and attribute to causal spans (KV cache, model forward, routing).
- Keep dashboards low-cost: pre-aggregated quantiles + top-k rollups instead of full tag explosion.
- Provide a short runbook so oncall can quickly escalate and triage.

Key signals & metric definitions (canonicalized):
- request_latency_ms_p50/p90/p95/p99: latency from API gateway ingress to final token stream close (ms).
- model_forward_ms_p50/p95/p99: time spent in model inference span (kernels + compilation) per request.
- kv_cache_latency_ms_p95: median+tail latency for KV cache lookup/restore.
- kv_cache_hit_rate: fraction of requests that get a prefix hit. Aggregated as top-level percent and per-shape top-k.
- batch_size_p50/p95: distribution of batch sizes at GPU; correlate with model_forward_ms.
- tenant_q95_share: fraction of global q95 latency contributed by a tenant (approximate attribution metric; see below).
- token_cost_per_request: token-based cost estimate (tokens + model multiplier) used for cost-SLO alignments.

Span attributes to instrument (required for trace-anchor strategy):
- span.name (e.g., api.request, router.route, model.forward, kv.lookup, kv.restore)
- trace.request_id (unique per API request)
- tenant_id (low-cardinality alias for top-K only; use hashed_topN to limit cardinality)
- model.name, model.variant, sequence_length, prompt_length, response_tokens
- kv_cache_hit (boolean), kv_key_checksum (short hash), kv_prefix_length
- batch_size (int), gpu_id, region, routing_policy (latency/cost)
- error.code (if applicable), fallback_reason (e.g., capacity, model_unavailable)

Trace-anchor technique (summary):
1) Identify the quantile regression window (time range and quantile that deviated).
2) Query top-N slow requests by latency (e.g., top 500 by request_latency_ms over the window).
3) For each trace, extract the dominant span pattern fingerprint: sequence of span names and key boolean attributes (e.g., model.forward + kv.restore(true) + batch_size<=1).
4) Group traces by fingerprint and compute group statistics: count, median/95/99 latencies, top tenants, model variants.
5) Surface top fingerprints in a dashboard widget with drill links to traces and to per-tenant attribution.

Why fingerprints? They compress high-cardinality traces into few patterns so we can find recurring tail causes (cold kv restore, small-batch model forward, bad routing hop). We avoid storing full high-cardinality label sets in metrics.

Dashboard panel specs (compact list):
- Quantile overview (time series): request_latency_p50/p90/p95/p99 as stacked quantile bands. Annotations for deploys/rollouts.
- Q95 attribution bar: top-20 tenants by q95_share (computed via sum of top-k slow requests weighted by latency).
- Fingerprint ranker: list of trace fingerprints with columns [fingerprint_id, example_span_sequence, count, q99_latency, dominant_tenant, dominant_model]. Each row links to a trace sample.
- Hotspot heatmap: model_variant x batch_size buckets showing p95 model_forward_ms.
- KV heatmap: kv_prefix_length x kv_cache_hit showing p95 kv_latency.
- Top slow traces table: top 200 slow traces (time, latency, tenant, fingerprint_id) with quick actions (open trace, add tenant to watchlist).
- Cost/latency scatter: token_cost_per_request vs request_latency to find expensive slow tails.

Queries & sketches (pseudo-SQL / PromQL ideas):
- Approximate tenant_q95_share:
  WITH top_slow AS (SELECT request_id, tenant_id, request_latency_ms FROM requests WHERE ts BETWEEN $start AND $end ORDER BY request_latency_ms DESC LIMIT 500)
  SELECT tenant_id, SUM(request_latency_ms) / (SELECT SUM(request_latency_ms) FROM top_slow) AS share FROM top_slow GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY share DESC LIMIT 20;

- Fingerprint extraction (pseudo-step): for trace in top_slow_traces: fingerprint = hash(join(span.name + ':' + (kv_cache_hit? 'KV1':'KV0') + ':' + floor(batch_size/4)))

Sampling & retention guidance:
- Retain full traces for 7 days by default, 30 days for onboarded enterprise tenants (compliance permitting).
- For production cost control: capture detailed tenant_id only for traces in top 1% latency or pre-flagged tenants; otherwise replace tenant_id with hashed_top1000 tag.
- Store fingerprint metadata (fingerprint_id -> example trace id, counts, dominant tenant) in a small index updated by a nightly job.

Alerting suggestions (starter rules):
- Alert A: global_q95 > baseline_q95 * 1.5 for 15m AND q95_increase_from_top3_tenants < 0.3 -> investigate infra/region/model stack (possible routing/regression).
- Alert B: any fingerprint group with count>50 and group_q99 > historical_group_q99 * 1.4 -> page oncall and attach top-trace sample.
- Alert C: kv_cache_hit_rate_global drops >10% in 5m -> create SEV-3; investigate cache eviction syncronization across nodes.

Runbook (triage steps):
1) Confirm metric: verify which quantile moved and for how long. Look at annotated deploys/rollouts.
2) Open fingerprint ranker and identify top fingerprint(s) by count and tail impact.
3) For top fingerprints, check dominant_tenant and model_variant. If dominated by a single tenant, temporarily throttle or route tenant to dedicated capacity (if available) while investigating.
4) Open model_forward spans for sample traces. Check batch_size distribution and GPU metrics for spikes.
5) If kv.restore spans present and slow, look at kv prefix length and recent cache evictions; correlate with shard-level metrics.
6) Document findings in incident note and create follow-up action (e.g., improved cache keying, batcher throttles, model quantization rollback).

Engineering instrumentation requests (minimal):
- Add fingerprint hashing function to trace consumer that runs for top-latency traces only. Store fingerprint in a lightweight metric tag (fingerprint_id) limited to top-500 fingerprint values.
- Emit kv_cache_hit boolean and kv_prefix_length as integer. 
- Ensure request_id and trace sampling decisions are propagated across routing hops.

Operational cautions & open questions:
- CardinaLITY: tenant_id is high-cardinality; avoid direct metric tag explosion. We use hashed_topN and a nightly top-tenants list.
- Attribution accuracy: using top-N slow traces biases toward large requests; consider normalizing by request count for fairness.
- Sampling bias: if traces are sampled probabilistically, ensure sampling is skew-aware (ensure higher sampling for slow/failed requests).

Next steps & action items (who/when):
- Jordan Lee: prototype fingerprint index job and small dashboard widget (2 weeks).
- Priya Nair: add kv_cache_hit + kv_prefix_length to model tracer (1 sprint).
- Diego Morales: draft alert thresholds and test runbook in tabletop (next oncall rotation).

Notes & references:
- Related confluence: OBS-quantile-sli-2025 (link above).
- See JIRA OBS-4827 for the fingerprint indexing task.

If you use this playbook during a triage, add a short note to the fingerprint index (update dominant_tenant or dominant_model) so future runs get smarter.
